about.title: Personal Injury Help in La Palma, California
about.longDescription: La Palma is a small, tightly-knit city in Orange County, but its streets still see their share of collisions. Recent public records show 64 injury collisions in a single year, with 91 people hurt and one traffic death — numbers that remind us accidents can happen to anyone, even on quiet neighborhood streets. Corridors like La Palma Avenue, Walker Street, and Orangethorpe Avenue see steady traffic volume, and reported crashes tend to cluster on Thursday afternoons between 5 and 7 p.m., a stretch when commuters and after-school traffic overlap. If you or someone you love was injured in a wreck on any of these roads, or anywhere else in the city, it helps to understand your options early. LawProactive is not a law firm — we're a free service that listens to what happened and connects you with an independent personal injury attorney who can review your situation. There's no cost to talk with us, and the attorneys in our network only get paid if they recover money for you. You don't have to figure this out alone, and you don't have to pay anything upfront to get answers about your claim.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Sooner Rather Than Later

items.title: California's Filing Deadline Is Real
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of an injury to file a claim in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity was involved. Waiting too long can cost you the right to recover anything at all.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you were partly responsible for the crash, you can still recover a share of damages. An attorney can help sort out how fault affects your specific claim.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In most ordinary injury cases, California places no limit on non-economic damages like pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life. That matters when injuries affect your daily routine long after the crash.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Unless You Win
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no upfront cost and no fee unless they recover money on your behalf. That structure lets you focus on healing instead of legal bills.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in La Palma?
items.answer: Under California law, you generally have two years from the date of injury to file most personal injury claims. If a government agency was involved in the crash, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's wise to get advice early.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault system, so being partially responsible doesn't automatically bar you from recovering compensation. Your recovery may be reduced by your share of fault, but you can still pursue a claim.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in La Palma?
items.answer: Public records show higher collision counts along corridors like La Palma Avenue, Walker Street, and Orangethorpe Avenue, with reported crashes tending to peak on Thursdays between 5 and 7 p.m. These are simply reported counts, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Do I have to pay anything upfront to speak with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if they recover money for you. There's no cost or obligation to have your case reviewed.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?
items.answer: No, LawProactive is not a law firm. We're a free connection service that helps injured people in La Palma and across Orange County get in touch with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate their situation.
